overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting a February 28 notice without discussion topics, in a non-24-hour location, and without recording the posting date and time; it found no violation on document or minutes timing.

allegations.summary: The notice for the February 28 meeting listed no discussion topics.
allegations.key_passage: The only version of the notice posted on bulletin board—the Town's official notice posting location at the time—was the preliminary notice which did not include a list of anticipated discussion topics or the date and time that the town clerk posted it.

allegations.summary: The February 28 meeting notice was posted on a Town Hall bulletin board not visible to the public at all hours.
allegations.key_passage: as the Committee acknowledges, the bulletin board at Town Hall did not comply with the Open Meeting Law's requirement that notices be posted in a manner conspicuously visible to the public 24 hours a day.

allegations.summary: The notice did not conspicuously record the date and time it was posted.
allegations.key_passage: The only version of the notice posted on bulletin board—the Town's official notice posting location at the time—was the preliminary notice which did not include a list of anticipated discussion topics or the date and time that the town clerk posted it.

allegations.summary: The Committee failed to timely publish documents and exhibits used at the February 28 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require the publication of minutes or documents used during a meeting.

allegations.summary: The Committee failed to timely publish (approve) minutes from its 2017 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We find this to be an appropriate amount of time for approving those minutes and therefore find no violation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's notice requirements
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
